skill.name: x402socks
skill.description: Discover regional proxy exits, quote USDC access on Base, and configure x402socks clients with spending approval and credential-handling guidance.
skill.summary: Manage paid regional proxy access through x402, with helper commands for discovery, quotes, token checks, and egress testing.
skill.author: x402socks

security_audit.summary: Most alerts concern benign documentation or expected credential handling; no evidence of malicious intent or prompt injection was found in the reviewed files. Confirmed risks include plaintext proxy authentication, incomplete payment authorization checks, and exit-identifier injection into curl configuration. Rotation and recovery also discard replacement responses, risking access loss.

remediation.issue: Reusable proxy credentials cross plaintext SOCKS5 and HTTP CONNECT hops.
remediation.suggestion: Default the helper and examples to verified TLS CONNECT endpoints. Require explicit opt-in for plaintext transport and explain credential interception risks.

remediation.issue: Payment approval does not constrain all signed authorization fields or alternative requirements.
remediation.suggestion: Validate network, asset, recipient, scheme, and amount at signing time. Bind the signer to the validated requirement and reject unapproved alternatives.

remediation.issue: The exit argument can add curl configuration options.
remediation.suggestion: Accept only validated exit identifiers from the current node feed. Reject quotes, newlines, and unexpected characters before generating curl configuration.

remediation.issue: Rotation and recovery responses are replaced by the Python heredoc on stdin.
remediation.suggestion: Use python3 -c or a separate parser script so stdin remains the response stream. Test replacement-token persistence and redaction before advertising safe rotation.

remediation.issue: The private-file status example embeds unescaped JSON in curl configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Escape configuration values using the helper's cfg_escape pattern, or send the JSON body through a separate private file.

semantic_findings.title: Payment Guard Does Not Bind the Full Authorization
semantic_findings.description: The TypeScript guard checks only accepts[0] for network and amount, then returns all requirements unchanged. Asset, recipient, and the signer's selected requirement are not bound to approval, allowing substituted authorization terms.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The supplied guard has no asset or recipient policy and does not constrain remaining requirements. Exploitation depends on substituted server requirements and client selection.

semantic_findings.title: Exit Identifier Can Inject Curl Configuration
semantic_findings.description: The test command inserts an unchecked exit identifier into a quoted curl configuration entry. Quotes and newlines can introduce another proxy option, redirecting reusable proxy credentials to an attacker-controlled proxy.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: exit_id comes directly from the command argument and is not escaped or validated before curl parses it. Credential values are escaped, but the proxy identifier is not.

semantic_findings.title: Rotation and Recovery Discard Replacement Credentials
semantic_findings.description: store_token_response uses stdin for a Python heredoc, leaving sys.stdin.read() empty instead of reading the piped response. Rotation can invalidate the existing token without saving its one-time replacement, disrupting access.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The heredoc replaces pipeline stdin for python3 -, so its later response read reaches EOF. Both rotation and recovery pipe responses into this function.

semantic_findings.title: Documented Status Configuration Does Not Escape JSON
semantic_findings.description: The safer status example embeds serialized JSON directly inside a quoted curl configuration value. Unescaped JSON quotes break that value, so the documented credential-validation request does not reliably send the intended body.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: json.dumps emits double quotes, and printf places them inside another quoted curl option without escaping. The helper script uses cfg_escape, but this example does not.

content.user_title: Configure Regional Proxy Access with x402socks
content.value_statement: Regional network testing requires proxy access, payment approval, and careful credential handling. This skill provides x402 purchase guidance, discovery commands, and client configuration examples.
actual_capabilities: Query service health and list healthy, enabled proxy exits.
Read the package catalog and display package prices and entitlements.
Decode live x402 payment challenges and compare quoted amounts with an optional spending cap.
Save proxy tokens locally and request token status or validation.
Provide curl, Python, Node, and browser proxy configuration examples.
Document wallet payment signing, token rotation, settlement recovery, and connection troubleshooting.
limitations: Purchases require approved spending, a funded Base wallet, and additional payment libraries; the shell helper does not purchase access.
SOCKS5 authentication is unencrypted, and the provided payment guard does not validate every authorization field.
Rotation and recovery helpers currently discard response input, preventing reliable replacement-token storage.
Prices, healthy exits, quotas, and target-site access depend on external services; proxy use does not guarantee anonymity or bypass permission requirements.

use_cases.title: Check Regional Application Behavior
use_cases.description: Compare your application from available regional exits after confirming transport security and approving any required purchase.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Agent Network Failures
use_cases.description: Check service health, token validity, exit availability, and connection symptoms before considering another paid package.

use_cases.title: Prototype Budgeted x402 Access
use_cases.description: Study the payment challenge and design signing checks that enforce the approved amount, asset, recipient, and network.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Available Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Check x402socks health, available exits, and current packages. Do not access my wallet or purchase anything.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Spending Approval
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the cheapest package suitable for my regional test. Show its live challenge amount and entitlements, then wait for my approval.

prompt_templates.title: Configure a Protected Connection
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure a healthy TLS CONNECT exit using my existing token file. Keep credentials out of arguments and output, and report the observed egress IP.

prompt_templates.title: Review Payment and Recovery Safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my x402 integration before execution. Verify signing-time approval checks, selected requirements, token persistence, and settlement recovery without making payments or rotating credentials.

output_examples.input: Show a purchase approval summary without paying.
output_examples.output: Illustrative approval summary: a six-hour package covers a short test. Confirm the current challenge amount and usage limits before approving payment.

output_examples.input: Explain the connection diagnostic result without showing credentials.
output_examples.output: Illustrative diagnostic: token validation succeeded, but the selected exit is unavailable. Choose a healthy exit with TLS CONNECT before retrying.

output_examples.input: What should happen after payment settles but provisioning fails?
output_examples.output: Do not purchase again. Retain the settlement transaction hash and use wallet-signed recovery after correcting the helper response-handling issue.

best_practices: Approve a specific maximum and validate the exact network, asset, recipient, and amount immediately before signing.
Prefer TLS CONNECT, restrict token-file permissions, and keep credentials out of process arguments, logs, and chat.
Refresh healthy exits and retain settlement evidence; verify replacement-token persistence before rotating or recovering credentials.
anti_patterns: Authorize purchases from a catalog quote alone or let a payment wrapper sign unchecked requirements.
Treat destination HTTPS as encryption for SOCKS5 authentication, or pass unchecked exit text into curl configuration.
Repeat settled purchases or rely on the current rotation helper without verifying replacement-token storage.

faq.question: What does the skill require?
faq.answer: The helper needs a shell, curl, and Python 3. Purchases also need payment libraries and a Base wallet funded with USDC.

faq.question: Does the shell helper buy a package?
faq.answer: No. It retrieves quotes and manages supporting operations. Purchase examples use separate x402 libraries and require explicit spending approval.

faq.question: Are prices and exits fixed?
faq.answer: No. Read the live catalog and node feed. Validate the actual payment challenge again before signing.

faq.question: Does SOCKS5 protect my token on the network?
faq.answer: No. SOCKS5 authentication sends credentials without encryption. Prefer TLS CONNECT on port 3129 where available.

faq.question: Where should I store the proxy token?
faq.answer: Use the application token file with mode 0600 or its named environment variable. Never include tokens in logs, arguments, or chat.

faq.question: Can I rely on the rotation and recovery helper?
faq.answer: Not currently. Its response parser loses piped input. Correct and test token persistence before using these operations, especially rotation.
